# Setting Up an Epson SureLab Print Controller

OrderHub Desktop (OHD) sends jobs to an Epson SureLab by writing an **order folder** into the hot folder that the Epson order software watches. Each order folder holds the images and a small **DPOF** instruction file that tells the printer the size, channel and number of copies for each image.

This article covers:

- adding an Epson SureLab controller;
- what every setting does;
- telling OHD which channel and print size each product uses (**Channel Mappings**);
- splitting large jobs into batches.

![Order Controllers](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/af4da3c1-38ca-4bd3-976c-09483f9c64e9.png)

---

## Before You Start

* The Epson order software must already be watching a hot folder, and the OHD computer must be able to write to it.
* Your channels must already be set up on the printer, one for each product and finish. You'll need each channel's number.

---

## Adding the Controller

1. In OHD, go to **Settings → Routing**.
2. In the **Order Controllers** section, click **+ Add Controller**. The **Add Controller** window opens.
3. In **Name**, type a name you'll recognise, for example **Epson SureLab**.
4. In **Type**, choose **Epson Surelab (DPOF)**.
   * Note: a new controller opens as **Noritsu (DPOF)**, so always change the **Type** first.
5. Next to **Output Path**, click **Browse...** and choose the Epson hot folder.
6. Fill in the rest of the settings (explained below), then click **Save Controller**.

![Edit Epson Controller](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/41bfc3de-f0a4-4d4c-96b3-9df1368b2bca.png)

Once saved, the controller appears as a card in **Order Controllers**, with **Edit**, **Duplicate** and **Delete** buttons and an **Auto Print** tick box.

* Note: deleting a controller also removes all of its **Process Routing** and **Channel Mappings** entries.

---

## The Settings

### Output Path

The hot folder the Epson order software watches. OHD writes one order folder here for each job.

### Auto Print — Send jobs to print automatically

When ticked, jobs for this controller are sent to the printer as soon as they're ready. When unticked, they wait for you to click **Process**. You can also turn this on and off with the **Auto Print** tick box on the controller's card.

### Check Order Status

* **Ticked:** when OHD sends a job, it moves to **In Production** in OrderHub and stays there. Sending a job to the printer doesn't mean the prints are finished, so OHD doesn't complete it. You complete the job in OrderHub as usual, and OHD follows.
* **Unticked:** the job still moves to **In Production** as soon as the order folder is written, but OHD doesn't watch the hot folder after that. You complete the job in OrderHub as usual.

* Note: if a job doesn't print, check the Epson order software. In the hot folder, an order folder whose name starts with **q** means the Epson software had a problem with it.

### Include customer surname in folder name

Adds the customer's surname to the order folder's name, between the job number and the product, for example `o38461218_PXDEMO-DR2PE0-1_Charnley_4x6 Photo Print`. This makes orders easier to find in the Epson software. If OHD can't work out a surname, it uses the full name.

### Maximum prints per job (optional)

Splits a large job into smaller batches so one big job doesn't hold up the printer. Each batch is sent as its own order folder, with its batch number in the folder name (for example **1of3**, **2of3**, **3of3**). The limit counts prints, not images: an image with 4 copies counts as 4. Copies of the same photo are always kept in the same batch. Leave blank for no limit.

**Send batches automatically**: Off: a large job waits for you to check it, then **Process** splits and sends it. On: large jobs don't wait — with Auto Print on, they're split and sent straight away.

* Note: this box is greyed out until you set a maximum.
* Note: a large job that's waiting shows **Large job — review required** in the Jobs list.

---

## Telling OHD Which Channel to Use: Channel Mappings

The controller tells OHD **where** to send a job. **Channel Mappings** tell it **how** to print each product: which channel on the printer, and what print size.

### How a job finds its controller

1. **Process Routing** (in **Settings → Routing**) sends each process type to a controller. For example, all **Photo Print** jobs go to **Epson SureLab**.
2. **Channel Mappings** then match the job's product code, and optionally its options, to a channel number and print size on that controller.

### Adding a mapping from a job (the easy way)

When a job arrives for a product that has no mapping yet, it shows an **Assign** button in the Jobs list instead of **Process**.

1. Click **Assign**. The **Assign Channel** window opens, showing the job's **Product**, **Product Code**, **Controller** and **Options**.
2. In **Channel Number**, type the channel set up on the printer for this product and finish, for example **12**.
3. In **Print Size Code**, type the print size. You can use a standard code such as **KG** (6×4), **2L** (5×7) or **A4**, or just type a size such as **4x6** and OHD will format it for the printer.
4. Optional: tick **Skip Auto Print** if jobs on this channel should always wait for you to click **Process**.
5. Click **Save & Assign**. OHD shows **Channel mapping saved — job is ready to print**.

Every later job with the same product and options uses this mapping automatically.

![Epson Assign Channel](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/7ebb622a-2b34-4c5b-9d69-61d8674486d8.png)

### Managing mappings in Settings

In **Settings → Routing → Channel Mappings**, you can add, edit and delete mappings. The **Add Channel Mapping** window has the same fields, plus **Controller**, **Product Code** and **Options (name : value pairs)**.

* Note: **Channel Number** and **Print Size Code** are both required.
* Note: tick **Ignore** on an option to skip it when matching jobs. It applies to every mapping on this controller, so jobs whose value for that option varies still match.
* Note: if a mapping is missing its print size, affected jobs show a **Fix mapping** button that opens it for you.

---

## What You'll See in the Hot Folder

Each job arrives as a folder whose name starts with **o**, for example `o38461218_PXDEMO-DR2PE0-1_Charnley_4x6 Photo Print`. It contains the images and the **DPOF.001** instruction file.

The Epson software usually renames the folder once it has dealt with it: a name starting with **e** means it took the order, and **q** means there was a problem.

* Reprints from Job Review go to the same hot folder as a new order folder, with **r1**, **r2** and so on in the name.
* Batches of a split job have **1of3**, **2of3** and so on in the name.

![Processed Epson Order](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/0c36b636-739a-4804-8e02-9d814ceacb0b.png)

---

## Good to Know

* Channel numbers and print sizes must match the printer's setup. Most "printed on the wrong paper or size" problems are a wrong channel number in a mapping.
* To use the same settings on a second Epson, click **Duplicate** on the controller's card, rename it and change the **Output Path**. **Duplicate** doesn't copy **Process Routing** or **Channel Mappings**.
* Changes to a controller or mapping apply to the next job sent. Orders already in the hot folder aren't affected.
